claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing revenue.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion.
AWS's AI business and its custom-silicon (chips) business each passed a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate.
The 2026 predictions in last year's edition of this piece held up; last year's edition predicted a cloud-first, AI-driven decade.
According to Gartner, by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027, and described cloud as becoming a business necessity.

McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report says cloud value driven by innovation is worth 5x more than cost savings, EBITDA uplift of 20–30% by 2030 for high-performing organizations, and Asia leads in projected cloud value followed by the US and Europe.
Hyperscalers are making the largest infrastructure investments in cloud history, nearly all centered on AI workloads, inference, and high-performance compute.
AWS posted $42.2 billion revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, per Amazon's Q2 2026 results release.
AWS's Q2 2026 growth of 37% accelerated from 28% growth the prior quarter, and was its fastest revenue growth since 2021.
AWS's AI business and chips business (including custom Trainium and Graviton silicon) are growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.

Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time, in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), with Azure revenue growing 43% year-over-year, up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said: "This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time."
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026, and its backlog reached $514 billion, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195–205 billion, up from an earlier $180–190 billion estimate that had already been raised twice this year.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year, with remaining performance obligations reaching $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year.
Oracle's RPO growth reflects large-scale AI infrastructure contracts, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals now totaling $75 billion.
Hybrid cloud will grow from $130B to $310–330B by 2030, per ResearchAndMarkets.
87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds, per Mordor Intelligence.
Gartner predicts that 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers found 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure, with most running more than one.
According to Gartner, total worldwide AI spending across software, hardware and services is forecast to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027, half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.
Enterprises are investing in GPU provisioning and orchestration, data pipelines, vector databases, feature stores and LLM infrastructure.
Pulumi Policies helps teams detect misconfigurations, analyze usage patterns, and generate infrastructure updates using AI-driven optimization.
Gartner predicts that by 2028, over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms to secure third-party AI service usage and protect custom-built AI applications.
Gartner predicts total spending on securing AI will reach roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
According to Gartner, by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams as internal providers of reusable services, components, and tools.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations have a dedicated platform engineering team and 35% are running a hybrid platform combining existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.

Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said: "Cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are not just experimenting but standardizing on CNCF projects that make software delivery reliable at scale... What's especially notable about this research is how organizations are extending those same platforms to support AI workloads, showing how cloud native is the base layer of powering the next era of applications."
Mid-size to large companies continue to invest in platform engineering practices, with large tech companies as first adopters.

Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029, while human-in-the-loop requirements in IT operations workflows fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 engineers, 82% agree that AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.

In Pulumi's 2026 survey, 63% say they trust agents to make production changes, yet manual approval remains close to universal today; Pulumi's report describes this as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, the share of teams expecting agents to generate half or more of their infrastructure code rises from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails in place.
Pulumi's blog post 'The Agentic Infrastructure Era' argues that AIOps is headed toward a supervised agentic operating model rather than faster dashboards and alerting alone.
AIOps includes observability, automation, and real-time analytics bridging DevOps, SRE, and IT operations, and in 2027 those signals increasingly feed an agent empowered to act on them.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.
CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%.
CNCF's Q3 2025 report says 30% of backend developers use Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, a decline the report attributes to the technology's growing maturity.

Inference workloads powered by LLMs and GPUs now require low-latency execution closer to the user, pushing organizations to schedule AI pipelines across edge and core clusters, often using Kubernetes as the common control plane.
Pulumi published a comparison of Kubernetes IaC tools at /blog/best-kubernetes-iac-tools-2026/.
Operating Kubernetes effectively now depends on robust automation, strong security controls, and standardized delivery models.
AI-powered coding assistants like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code and Cursor have moved from novelty to everyday tooling for a large share of enterprise software teams.

According to Gartner, by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use dedicated AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use AI code assistants.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit.
Mirantis's Lens launched a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.
The July 2026 MCP revision is part of what makes direct action by AI assistants on infrastructure practical.
Pulumi Agent Skills is a collection of infrastructure expertise packaged for AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI, reducing hallucination and improving outputs.
Pulumi Agent Skills is one of the newest developments (recently released).
Pulumi has a Remote MCP Server, and Pulumi Neo executes actions with previews, policies, and orchestration.
AI code assistants are fast becoming a competitive advantage in cloud software development.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
Modern IaC, unified governance, reusable components, and policy frameworks are all core capabilities of the Pulumi Cloud platform.
The post is titled and framed as the trends shaping 2027 and beyond, while the file path and image paths reference 2024.
AI agents are moving from writing code to operating infrastructure directly, with humans approving changes rather than authoring every one.
